The best chain is QB7-QB12-QB11, with QB12 in the middle. I read the default calibration set of the real garnet QPU (f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade). All 28 calibrated CZ pairs have a valid IRB fidelity in the slepian_crf metric. The IRB CZ fidelity of QB7-QB12 is 0.998016 and the fidelity of QB12-QB11 is 0.998693. Their product is 0.996712. The next best chain is QB12-QB11-QB16, with a product of 0.994689.

I ran a 3-qubit GHZ circuit on garnet:mock with 200 shots. It used native gates only. Job ID: 01a15fa2-4fa0-72cf-81f1-bb698a0da016. The mock used calibration set f04fe114-002f-46bd-8fa4-2a577ff56501. The circuit applies RY(pi/2) to QB12. It then builds CNOT QB12->QB7 from RY(pi/2), CZ on (QB12,QB7) and RY(-pi/2). It builds CNOT QB12->QB11 the same way, with CZ on (QB12,QB11). It has no other CZ gates. It measures all 3 qubits under key m, in the order (QB7, QB12, QB11). The leftmost bit is QB7.

The job completed with counts 000: 49, 001: 46, 110: 51, 111: 54, for 200 shots in total. The mock returns random results, so these counts do not show a real GHZ state. The job never ran on the real garnet QPU, so it used no QPU credits.
